explanations: getJob calls fetch directly instead of going through request(), so it has no AbortSignal timeout (and network errors escape as raw errors rather than retryable TranscoderErrors). If Encoda accepts the connection but stalls, the await never settles; because tick() processes jobs sequentially and guards with the running flag, every later tick returns immediately and no asset is ever marked ready or failed again until the process restarts.

submit sends Idempotency-Key: asset-<assetId>, which is the same on every retry for that asset, so a provider honoring the header returns the original job. A fresh key per call would cause duplicates; nothing here throws non-retryable on a retry.

assertOk throws TranscoderError with retryable = false for 404 (not 429 or 5xx). checkOne catches it and, since it is non-retryable, calls markFailed, then continues with the next job. Retryable errors are the ones left pending.
toJob converts the provider's bits-per-second value with Math.round(o.video_bitrate / 1000), giving 4500 kbps. The raw value is not stored as-is and no rendition is filtered out.
